To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cd incorporation by Si-rich matrixes (silica fume and α-Quartz) was more energetics favored by silica fume.
Cd can be effectively incorporated into silica fume and quartz matrices by forming cadmium silicates at temperatures above 700 °C.
Cd incorporation by silica fume was more energetics favored than that by quartz.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (1) the efficiency of Cd immobilization by two types of Si-rich matrices, (2) reaction mechanisms of Cd immobilization, and (3) leachability of cadmium silicates.
the development of a new technology for cadmium detoxifying and immobilization.
the stabilization of cadmium via the formation of silicates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cd incorporation into crystalline silicates was more efficient than the incorporation into amorphous silicates.
CdSiO 3 is a promising Cd-stabilizing agent, and Cd2SiO 4 and Cd3 SiO 5 are less preferable than CdSiO  3.

Cd incorporation by silica fume was more energetics favorable than Cd incorporation by α-quartz, and the sintering temperature was an important processing parameter to control the formation of cadmium silicates and their leaching behaviors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cd stabilization via Si-rich matrices is feasible and the Cd leachability is highly dependent on the Cd incorporation products and the leachant.
CdSiO4 and α-quartz were the most effective Cd-hosting product and Si-rich matrix, respectively.
Cd2SiO3 and Cd3Si2O7 were formed in Г = 1.0 and Г = 2.0 systems at temperatures above 1000 °C, whereas Cd3SiO3 was dominant at temperatures below 1000 °С in Г =1.0 system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CdSiO 3 is a more effective Cd-hosting product than Cd2Si O 4 and Cd 3Si O 5 in terms of Cd immobilization.
the use of silica fume as a Cd-hosting matrix is a promising strategy for cadmium immobilization.
